evals.prompt: Audit this macOS SwiftUI window for Liquid Glass violations. Do not edit anything.
evals.expected_output: Produces a read-only violation report that classifies every region as content or functional, names the mechanism behind each violation rather than only the rule, checks container batching, modifier order, corner concentricity, tint count, and symbol availability against the deployment target, and edits nothing.

evals.prompt: Add a floating zoom control cluster over the canvas in this macOS app.
evals.expected_output: Walks the decision order before writing glass, records why no standard component suffices, places the cluster in the functional layer inside a single GlassEffectContainer, derives its shape concentrically rather than hard-coding a radius, tints at most one prominent action, and records the substitution under Reduce Transparency and Reduce Motion.

evals.prompt: Make the record rows in this table look premium by giving each row a glass card background.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the content-layer glass, cites the normative rule and the compositing mechanism that breaks scroll edge effects and light/dark adaptation, notes the unbounded render-pass cost of per-row effects, and offers standard content materials plus a functional-layer alternative instead.

evals.prompt: Use glassBackgroundEffect and .rect(corner: .containerConcentric) for this Mac panel, and mark the AppKit glass view interactive.
evals.expected_output: Rejects all three: glassBackgroundEffect is visionOS only, .rect(corner: .containerConcentric) is not SwiftUI API and containerConcentric is the UIKit and AppKit spelling, and NSGlassEffectView.effectIsInteractive is macOS 27 beta with no macOS 26 equivalent; supplies the correct SwiftUI ConcentricRectangle and Edge.Corner.Style spellings and an availability guard.
